summary: Bryantsville (Georgia), Lawrence County, Indiana: a Hoosier National Forest lookout reportedly dismantled in 1972; the footers were still there in June 2024.

facts.design: Four angle-iron legs set in deep concrete, seven-by-seven-foot cab; said to be 100 feet tall
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1972 according to Indiana Fire Towers, citing a 2013 Outdoor Indiana article; footers still exist as of June 2024.

access.note: On Hoosier National Forest property. A gravel forest road is said to lead toward the old lookout site.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The gravel road that starts where the pavement ends is said to lead to the old lookout site and a radio tower.

facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Hoosier National Forest

events.note: 1949 topographic map shows the lookout tower but not the radio tower

1965 topographic map shows a radio tower southwest of the lookout site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Indiana Fire Towers says both names are used. The Forest Service table lists a Bryantsville Tower and a Georgia Tower and calls them likely the same tower; the story treats them as one.
Indiana Fire Towers spells her first name other ways (Clarrisse, Clarissie). The Forest Service page and the 2025 report use Clarisse Carroll, which the story follows.

sources.title: Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: No source read gives a build date, so none is in the story. Indiana Fire Towers' 1936-map inference that the tower did not yet exist is speculation and is left out. The 1972 dismantling date rests on a 2013 magazine article cited second-hand. The Forest Service story Indiana Fire Towers cites is no longer online, so the Forest Service lookout-towers page is the reference used. Her name is spelled three ways across sources.
